ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed shareholders, directors, officers, authorized signatories and beneficial owners of the WFOE must be screened before filing against UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, PRC domestic terrorist designation lists, and PBOC high-risk money laundering and terrorist financing lists. PEP screening must cover foreign and domestic PEPs, their family members, and close associates using risk-based customer due diligence. Any PEP match or sanctions hit triggers enhanced due diligence, source of wealth verification, beneficial ownership re-piercing, senior management approval, and escalation to the AML compliance committee. Screening must be repeated at formation and every 90 days thereafter, with negative media and adverse information monitoring continuously documented.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration and Name Reservation Online System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE must adopt a standard simplified Chinese name using the four-tier naming convention: administrative division plus distinctive trade name plus industry or business scope plus corporate form. The English name, if registered, must be a phonetic or semantic transliteration of the Chinese name and must not conflict with prior registered names. Traditional Chinese characters, dialect characters, abbreviations, or non-standard romanization are not accepted for the statutory Chinese name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant has 15 working days from electronic notice to file an administrative reconsideration application with the superior SAMR or the designated internal appeal queue in the name reservation system. The appeal must state the legal basis, attach all previous rejection notices, explain why the proposed name is not misleading or prohibited, and propose a fallback name. If administrative reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit within six months. In parallel, counsel should immediately pre-reserve two alternative names through the online portal to prevent project delay and preserve the registration timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for this WFOE because the registered business is an airport bonded in-flight meal production kitchen requiring a physical, licensed production site, bonded inventory storage, and direct ramp delivery capability. The local SAMR will reject a virtual address for a food-manufacturing entity, the tax authority requires actual business premises for tax registration and invoice control, and Chinese banks will refuse to open corporate settlement accounts without a physical site inspection. A registered office must therefore be a real operating address satisfying food safety, customs supervision, and aviation security requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk: HIGH, approximately 85% likelihood of an unannounced joint inspection within the first 12 months of incorporation. Inspection checklist: verify legal representative and staff presence; confirm the registered address matches the actual kitchen; inspect food production license, staff health certificates, and hygiene records; verify payroll and social security headcount; review bonded inventory and in-flight meal storage; inspect ramp delivery vehicles and aviation security protocols; reconcile bank receipts with declared revenue and tax filings. Municipal SAMR, tax, customs, and food safety officers may conduct simultaneous unannounced inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan (as amended), particularly Articles 2, 6, 98 to 108 (Limited Company), 128, 129, 156 to 158 (share capital and shares), 172, 202, 208 and 210 (board of directors, chairperson and corporate governance); Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 4 to 8; Regulations on Company Registration; Regulations on Fees for Company Registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, Company Registration Division, Taiwan.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application and Company Registration Certificate (filed through the Company and Commercial Registration Central Application Portal).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No fixed statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a limited company under the Company Act of Taiwan. However, the WFOE must have paid-in capital reasonably commensurate with its approved investment amount and the ISIC 5621 inflight catering business scope, and the capital must be remitted into a Taiwan bank capital contribution account, verified by a certified public accountant, and reported on the capital verification report. There is no mandatory blocked escrow account requirement for a standard WFOE; the foreign exchange control regime requires the capital to be used only for the investment purpose approved by the Investment Commission, and any diversion requires prior approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED. RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY BY THE FOUNDING DIRECTORS of the Company, duly convened at the registered office on the date first written above, with the attendance of the full board and the consent of the sole shareholder, and in accordance with Articles 172, 202 and 208 of the Company Act of Taiwan: 1. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company shall be established at [Insert full Taiwan street address] and the Company Secretary is instructed to notify the Ministry of Economic Affairs and the local municipal government and to maintain all legal records at such address. 2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The sole founder subscribes to the entire authorized share capital of NT$[insert] divided into [insert] ordinary shares of par value NT$10 each. The full subscription price shall be paid in cash into a Taiwan bank account duly opened in the Company's name. The mandated certified public accountant shall prepare a capital verification report for attachment to the incorporation registration. The Chief Financial Officer is hereby authorized to accept the subscription, issue the share certificates, and execute any remittance and escrow directions. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The operational, payroll, and inflight contract accounts shall be opened at [Bank and Branch]. Each of the Chairperson and the Financial Controller is authorized, jointly in pairs, to open such accounts, sign checks, initiate wire transfers, execute receipts, and negotiate banking facilities, with such specimen signatures to be supplied to the bank. 4. STATUTORY OFFICERS APPOINTMENT. The following officers are appointed: [Name] Chairperson and legal representative; [Name] General Manager; [Name] Chief Financial Officer; [Name] Company Secretary and Compliance Officer. Each officer shall have authority to bind the Company within the limits of ordinary corporate powers and as separately approved by the board. 5. IMPLEMENTATION AND DELEGATION. The General Manager and Company Secretary are jointly and severally authorized to prepare, execute and file the incorporation registration application with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, to obtain foreign investment approval documents, to make necessary statutory declarations, and to procure the industrial and food-related operating licenses required for the inflight catering kitchen. This resolution is irrevocable until the board revokes or amends it in writing, and shall be submitted as a corporate record to the competent authority upon request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Negative List Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA-IC), via Global Investment and Business E-Service portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the foreign investment application in the name of the ultimate foreign beneficial owner. The application must identify the proposed WFOE, the total and source of foreign currency capital, the intended registered address, the proposed directors and the ISIC 5621 inflight catering business scope. The Investment Commission will screen the activity against Taiwan's foreign investment negative list and, if cleared, will issue a Foreign Investment Approval Letter authorizing the remittance of capital and the company incorporation. The approval letter must be appended to the later company registration filing. All supporting documents submitted from abroad must be notarized or legalized, and a power of attorney from the foreign investor must be apostilled if the investor is in a Hague Apostille member jurisdiction. Any discrepancy in the shareholding structure or source of funds must be cured before the equity capital is wired.
required_dossiers: Application form for investment by foreign nationals
Authenticated certificate of incorporation and good standing of the foreign investing entity
Latest audited financial statements of the foreign investor
Certified copy of the ultimate beneficial owner's identity document
Investment plan and proposed WFOE articles of association
Power of attorney duly legalized or apostilled
Statement confirming no foreign investment negative list restriction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a supplemental query, respond within 30 days with a sworn explanation and corrected documents, or apply for a formal extension; if the investment is rejected on negative list grounds, restructure the business scope into permissible activities and file a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company and Commercial Registration Central Application Portal, Department of Commercial Affairs, MOEA.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the WFOE's proposed English and Chinese company name and the official Taiwan business scope code for catering, food manufacturing and air transport support activities. The company name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must not include words suggesting a government agency or regulated profession. A successful name reservation is valid for six months and may be extended once. The business scope must be drafted in the exact terminology used by the central registration database, including the production of meals for airlines and material supply to aircraft catering operations. Name and scope approval should be obtained before the articles are notarized, as the articles must mirror the approved scope exactly.
required_dossiers: Name pre-approval application
Foreign investment approval letter from MOEA-IC
Identity documents of the proposed local representative
Proposed English and Chinese registered name
Proposed Taiwan business scope classification codes
Registered office address consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for identical or confusing similarity, submit up to three alternative names in priority order on the same application; if the business scope is rejected, narrow or reclassify the scope code and resubmit with an explanatory statement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Capital Contribution Account, Remit Equity, and Obtain Certified Public Accountant Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan-chartered commercial bank and independent certified public accountant registered in Taiwan.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Investment Commission approval, the WFOE must open a capital contribution account in the proposed company name at a Taiwan-chartered bank. The foreign parent is required to remit the approved NT$ capital through an exchange bank, and the remittance certificate must be retained. The bank will issue a proof-of-deposit letter stating the account holder, the deposit date and the balance. The appointed certified public accountant must then issue a capital verification report certifying that the capital has been fully paid in cash, that no asset contribution has been overvalued, and that the shares have been validly subscribed. This report must be dated within fifteen days of the incorporation filing and must bear the CPA's registration seal. The bank and CPA are jointly responsible for identifying money-laundering red flags, so a clean source-of-funds statement from the foreign parent is essential.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment approval letter
Bank remittance and foreign exchange certificate
Proof-of-deposit letter from the Taiwan bank
Subscription agreement executed by the founder
Proposed articles of association
Certified passports or national IDs of the statutory officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the remittance is delayed by anti-money-laundering screening, provide the bank with an enhanced source-of-funds declaration and obtain a new release; if the CPA capital verification report is queried, have the accountant correct the report and reissue it with a current date before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Incorporation Registration and Obtain Company Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Registration Division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application online or at the MOEA service counter once the articles, name approval, capital verification report, foreign investment approval letter, registered office consent and officer consents are complete. The examiner will verify that the paid-in capital equals the approved investment amount, that the business scope is within the foreign investors negative list exemption, that the directors and supervisors are statutory eligible, and that the registered office is a lawful commercial address. If the examiner approves, the MOEA will issue the Company Registration Certificate and a unified business number, which authorizes the WFOE to commence administrative operations, open permanent bank accounts and apply for business licenses. The registered office must be physically ready for inspection at the time of application.
required_dossiers: Company Incorporation Registration Application form
Notarized or certified articles of association
First board resolution and shareholder consents
Certified public accountant capital verification report
Registered office consent, lease agreement and building usage certificate
Foreign investment approval letter from MOEA-IC
List of directors, supervisors and statutory officers
Power of attorney for the local filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner issues a formal deficiency notice, correct the stated items and resubmit within 15 days; if online filing is suspended, attend the MOEA service counter with original documents and request immediate re-examination or a written cure schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Tax Registration, Social Insurance Registration and Post-Formation Governance Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance), local Labor Insurance Administration, municipal Department of Economic Development, and local health bureau/food authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within fifteen days of the issuance of the Company Registration Certificate, the WFOE must apply to the National Taxation Bureau for the unified business number and tax registration, register as a withhold/reporting employer with the labor insurance and health insurance administrations, and notify the municipal economic development office of the intended factory installation. For the inflight catering kitchen, this step is part of the post-formation governance checklist: the board must formally adopt an internal compliance manual for food safety, occupational safety, and civil defense, and must designate a registered site manager with the required academic certificate. All statutory officer appointments in the first board resolution must be reflected on the tax and social insurance registrations, otherwise a separate amended registration would be necessary.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Articles of association and board resolution
Unified business number application forms
Foreign investment approval letter
Registered office lease or ownership certificate
Identity and household registration data of Taiwan statutory officers
Bank account confirmation of initial capital
Employment registration forms for planned employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late tax registration attracts a monetary fine; to cure, file immediately with a declaration and pay any assessed penalty; if the unified business number assignment fails due to a mismatch in company data, correct the underlying registration at MOEA before resubmitting to the National Taxation Bureau.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA) under the Ministry of Health and Welfare; Department of Economic Development of the local municipal government; Environmental Protection Administration; local Fire Bureau under the Fire Services Act.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Registration and Food Factory Registration under the Act Governing Food Safety and Sanitation; Factory Registration under the Factory Management Act; Aircraft Catering Operation Permission issued by the Civil Aviation Administration for ramp delivery, covering heat-retained, chilled and frozen meal assembly.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Taiwan, delegated to the municipal Environmental Protection Bureau.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration (Class 2 pollution prevention plan) for inflight catering kitchens with cooking capacity below the EIA threshold; a Full EIA Report (Category A or B) is mandatory when the kitchen is located in a designated environmentally sensitive area, when wastewater discharge design exceeds 100 cubic meters per day, or when the food production line includes hydrogenation, solvent extraction or waste-to-energy equipment. In standard airport industrial zones, the competent authority will require an Environmental Impact Sufficiency Review and a Pollution Prevention and Control Permit for fixed air emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from food processing and cleaning must satisfy the Taiwan effluent standards for the food industry: pH 6.0 to 9.0, biochemical oxygen demand not

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, acting through its Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax) portal and the Golden Tax Phase IV system for invoice clearance and tax supervision.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The CN WFOE obtains its legal status via the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) business license; under the integrated multi-license consolidation registration, SAMR data sharing auto-registers the WFOE with the STA and issues the tax Identification Number (TIN) equal to the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). The WFOE must then activate its tax account in the STA e-Tax portal, register financial and legal controllers, set up payroll and social insurance records, implement statutory accounting records, apply for VAT invoice quotas, complete VAT general taxpayer status determination, and register the bonded in-flight catering kitchen with China Customs for export supervision. For foreign non-resident entities without a permanent establishment in China, the statutory route is non-resident enterprise tax registration through the withholding agent or a tax representative before the STA, supported by foreign entity certificate and contractual documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under the Enterprise Income Tax Law; China does not offer check-the-box pass-through elections or elective hybrid mismatch treatment. The WFOE is a PRC resident enterprise taxed at entity level on worldwide income. A VAT general taxpayer/small-scale taxpayer election is available under the VAT regime but does not change entity-level EIT classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales is the mandatory threshold for general VAT taxpayer classification; every Chinese WFOE must complete VAT tax registration upon establishment regardless of turnover. Non-resident foreign suppliers making taxable supplies into China may have separate registration or withholding-agent collection obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates real-time fiscal control via the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform under Golden Tax Phase IV. VAT invoices must be issued from the tax authority-controlled system, uploaded to the STA for near-real-time clearance, and protected by a tax-control digital stamp, anti-counterfeit QR code, and centralized data matching. High-volume B2B issuers, including the inflight catering WFOE, are required to use API-based integration with the platform for automated invoice generation, routing, and reconciliation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies to goods physically exported from the PRC customs territory where the WFOE is the registered exporter, the goods are customs-declared for export, the export invoices are issued, the sales proceeds are received in foreign currency and repatriated within the statutory deadline, and the export documentation is complete. Inflight catering meals supplied from a bonded airport kitchen to international airlines may qualify for the export zero rate when the meals are loaded onto an outbound international flight under customs supervision and are consumed outside the PRC customs territory; domestic sales remain taxable at the applicable standard rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) filed through the China Customs Single Window for the international outbound movement
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exportation of the inflight catering cargo from the PRC customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or an equivalent State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) export foreign-exchange receipt record evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Export sales contract with the international airline or foreign purchasing entity
Commercial invoice, packing list, and export cargo manifest
Bonded warehouse entry/exit or customs supervision documentation for the airport inflight catering kitchen
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and China Customs jointly audit export zero-rating and refund claims. If the export declaration, transportation documents, invoice trail, bonded supervision records, or foreign-exchange repatriation evidence are missing, inconsistent, or false, the zero rate is denied, the VAT is retrospectively clawed back, and late-payment surcharge is imposed at 0.05% per day. A penalty of 50% to 500% of the under-collected tax may be applied under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection; fraudulent export refund claims may also trigger criminal liability under the Criminal Law, export-invoice restriction, downgrade of tax credit rating, and loss of export-tax-refund eligibility for the WFOE.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains partial capital account convertibility with current account transactions generally open. For WFOEs, profit remittance is permitted post-tax clearance and SAFE verification but subject to forex registration and source-of-funds documentation. Hurdles include SAFE approval thresholds for large outflows and potential delays in repatriation verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory timeline: Export receipts must be surrendered to the designated foreign exchange bank within 180 days. Mandatory conversion and surrender of 100% of export proceeds at the bank's prevailing exchange rate, unless exempted for specific trade financing with prior SAFE approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. Legal constraints: Offshore digital EMIs are restricted for corporate treasury functions under China's AML and FX regulations; local bank accounts with SWIFT connectivity are required for cross-border operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permitted for low-risk WFOE accounts with digital KYC, but physical presence of authorized signatories or directors is required for initial onboarding, high-value transactions, or if red flags are identified during verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership not fully disclosed or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declaration, corporate due diligence report, and notarized ownership chain

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent transaction patterns with declared business scope of airline inflight catering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business license, operational contracts with airlines, audited financials, and purpose-specific payment explanations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Use SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'Capital Injection' or 'Foreign Investment'. Verification requires SAFE filing for WFOE capital contribution and ongoing forex monitoring. Purpose codes must reference the ISIC 5621 airline catering scope.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: SWIFT MT103 for remittances, Commercial LC for larger deals. For aviation catering operations, employ correspondent banks with proper LC negotiation and payment instructions under UCP600.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate information report on directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding more than 10% of capital (Company Act Article 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Central Company Registration E-Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 1 to June 30 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine for late or false filing; compulsory filing order; persistent non-compliance may culminate in MOEA-ordered dissolution or deregistration of the WFOE.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular shareholders' approval of audited financial statements, business report, and profit-distribution proposal, followed by filing of meeting minutes and financial statements with MOEA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (minutes and approved financial statements filed within 30 days of shareholder approval)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting no later than June 30 following the fiscal year-end; MOEA filing by July 30 for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties imposed on responsible persons for failure to convene or approve; unapproved profit distribution is void; repeated default supports administrative dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax settlement return for profit-seeking enterprises, including audited profit and loss statement and related tax schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau under the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 through May 31 of the year following the taxable year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of assessed tax with statutory minimum; overdue-payment charges and monthly interest; understatement penalties; enforced levy on bank accounts and criminal referral for willful evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CPA-audited financial statements and auditor's report filed with the company register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Central Company Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after shareholder approval, normally on or before July 30 for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines on responsible persons under the Company Act; audit qualifications or profit distributions may be challenged; egregious failure may trigger MOEA-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual related-party transaction disclosure and transfer pricing documentation readiness schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (filed electronically with the annual CIT settlement return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the CIT settlement return by May 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Tax authority may recharacterize transactions at arm's-length consideration under Income Tax Act Article 43-1; additional tax, penalties up to twice the underpaid tax, and interest accrue.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Food business registration maintenance and annual HACCP/GHP or equivalent food-safety surveillance verification for the in-flight catering kitchen
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal health bureau and Taiwan Food and Drug Administration; accredited third-party certification bodies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Registration update within 15 days of any material change; annual surveillance audit completed before certificate expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under the Food Safety and Sanitation Act; suspension or revocation of food business registration; product recall orders; removal from airline catering vendor approval lists.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory CPA audit when paid-in capital reaches NT$30,000,000 (approximately USD 1,000,000) under Company Act Article 20 and MOEA order; audit also required when ordered by MOEA, the Financial Supervisory Commission, or a creditor, and is typically imposed by airline catering contract and airport concession covenants even below the statutory threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public WFOEs apply Taiwan EAS (Enterprise Accounting Standards) issued by the FSC, consistent with the Commercial Accounting Act and Income Tax Act; IFRS applies to public-interest entities. Note: Commercial Accounting Act Article 38 requires retention of ledgers and financial statements for at least 10 years and supporting vouchers for at least 5 years; the numeric field is expressed as a normalized pipeline value of 7.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan imposes no separate UBO registry for an in-flight catering WFOE; the annual confirmation is discharged through the Company Act Article 22-1 report filed between March 1 and June 30, which captures directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding more than 10% of capital. Every share transfer must be recorded in the share transfer book and in the Register of Members to be effective against the company; transfers attract securities transaction tax, and any transferee exceeding the 10% threshold must appear in the next annual Article 22-1 filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Supervisors (or equivalent board records)
Minute Book (shareholders' meeting and board meeting minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 to USD 1,000 per year for a registered office or local agent; full-service corporate secretarial retainer typically USD 1,500 to USD 3,500 per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 to USD 6,500 for a certified CPA audit, tax closing support, and related schedules for a private WFOE below the public-interest threshold
